# AP-SEC-003 Staff Access, Restricted Items, and Approvals

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes procedures for managing staff access to restricted areas and the handling of restricted items within AeroPolicy Airport. It outlines the roles and responsibilities for requesting access, approving restricted items, and ensuring compliance with security protocols. The policy applies to all staff members, including those working in landside, airside, and baggage make-up areas. It ensures that only authorized personnel may access restricted zones and that restricted items are handled in accordance with established procedures to maintain safety and operational integrity.

## 2. Staff Access Zones  
Staff access to restricted zones is strictly controlled and limited to authorized personnel. Landside areas are accessible to all staff with appropriate credentials. Airside areas, including runways, taxiways, and terminal airside zones, are restricted to authorized personnel only. The baggage make-up area is a controlled zone accessible to baggage handlers and authorized staff. Access to these zones is governed by individual role-based permissions and must be verified through the airport’s access control system. Unauthorized entry into restricted zones is prohibited and may result in disciplinary action.

## 3. Restricted Items  
Restricted items include, but are not limited to, tools, blades, lithium batteries, and flammable liquids. These items pose a risk to safety and security and must be handled with care. Staff must be aware of the types of restricted items and the conditions under which they may be transported or stored. All restricted items must be identified, logged, and stored in accordance with applicable regulations. Staff are required to report any restricted items found in their possession or in the workplace to the appropriate authority for review and action.

## 4. Approval Procedure for Restricted Items  
Approval to carry a restricted item airside must be granted in writing by the Security Duty Manager before the item passes the staff screening point. A Requesting Staff Member must submit a written request detailing the item, its purpose, and the intended location of use. The Line Manager must endorse the request to confirm its necessity and compliance with operational requirements. The Security Duty Manager reviews and approves the request based on risk assessment and security protocols. All approvals must be documented and retained for audit purposes. Unauthorized possession or transport of restricted items is strictly prohibited and may lead to disciplinary measures.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
A restricted item found in a checked bag must be handled in accordance with AP-BAG-001. The item must be isolated and secured to prevent access by unauthorized individuals. The incident must be reported under AP-INC-002 to ensure proper documentation and follow-up. Airport security personnel are responsible for coordinating with relevant authorities to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements. All actions taken in response to a restricted item found in baggage must be recorded and reviewed for effectiveness and compliance with security standards.

## 6. Records and Review  
All requests, approvals, and incident reports related to restricted items must be documented and retained for a minimum of two years. Records must be accessible for audit and review by authorized personnel. Regular reviews of access logs and restricted item handling procedures are conducted to ensure compliance with this policy and to identify areas for improvement. Staff are required to maintain accurate records of restricted items in their possession and to update them promptly. All records must be reviewed annually by the Security Duty Manager to ensure ongoing adherence to policy and regulatory requirements.
